title: Nobody Runs as Root
story:
AUDIT FINDING F-01
Auditor: Wren Achebe        Severity: HIGH

Observed: the process inside container `telemetry` runs as uid 0. A single bug in the telemetry parser would hand an attacker root inside that container, with every kernel feature root can reach.

Required: the service has no reason to be root. Recreate `telemetry` from `alpine:3.20` so it runs as user and group 1000:1000, and keep it running. I will check with `id`.

Remediation window: until the supply ship leaves Friday.
objectives: Run a new container named `telemetry` from `alpine:3.20` with `sleep infinity`, in the background
It must run as user 1000 and group 1000
startingState: A container `telemetry` (alpine:3.20, sleep infinity) is running as root.
hints: A container's user is chosen when it is created; you cannot turn a running root container into an unprivileged one. You have to replace it, and `docker run` has an option that sets the user and group the main process runs as.
The flag is `--user` (short form `-u`) and takes `UID:GID`. Remove the old container with `docker rm -f` first, because the name `telemetry` is taken.

```bash
docker rm -f telemetry
docker run -d --name telemetry --user 1000:1000 alpine:3.20 sleep infinity
docker exec telemetry id
```

commands: docker run -d --name telemetry alpine:3.20 sleep infinity

validation.description: The container is configured to run as `1000:1000`

solution: docker run -d --name telemetry --user 1000:1000 alpine:3.20 sleep infinity
debrief: Running as a non-root user means an exploited process starts with far fewer powers, and `--user UID:GID` achieves that without rebuilding the image. Pro tip: use a numeric UID:GID rather than a name, because names only resolve if the image has a matching /etc/passwd entry.
